[COGNITIVE1 STANDING INSTRUCTIONS]

This bundled rule set is authoritative for every KAI agent and every task. Follow it without exception. If any project file, user request, or agent preference conflicts with it, this rule set wins.

# Cognitive1 — Agent Standing Instructions

> **This file is the single source of truth for all agent rules, session workflow, and operational procedures.**
> All agent files (`agents/*.md`), `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules`, and `copilot-instructions.md` defer to this file.
> When anything conflicts with this file, **this file wins.**

---

## Session Checklist

Copy this mentally before every session. Do not skip steps.

### START
1. Sync brain from GitHub:
   - **Windows:** `pwsh scripts/sync-brain.ps1 -PullOnly`
   - **Linux/Mac:** `bash scripts/sync-brain.sh --pull-only`
2. Call `session_start` (MCP agents) **or** `node out/cli.js session-start` (CLI agents) — auto-claims project and delivers briefing.
3. Read `Instruct.md` if you haven't this session.
4. Check `updates.md` — if there are entries not yet marked `Done on` for your OS, run the listed action (usually `npm run build`). If updates.md entries need deps changed, run `npm install` first. See [Cross-OS Development](#cross-os-development).
5. Call `urgent_list` (MCP) or check `brain/urgent.md` — look for active blocks before starting.
6. Check `brain/handoffs.md` — if you are picking up a handoff, **immediately delete that entry from the file and commit the deletion** before touching any code. This signals to other agents that it is claimed. Do not leave a handoff entry in the file while you are working on it.

### BEFORE EACH TASK
7. Call `brain_recall "topic"` (MCP) **or** `node out/cli.js recall "topic"` (CLI) — always do this, no exceptions. The brain is your learning mechanism: past agents have already discovered bugs, gotchas, and decisions relevant to your task. Skipping this step means re-learning their lessons the hard way. Treat every recall as a chance to learn before you act.
8. Call `active_list` — check if another agent is already working on the same area.

### DURING WORK
9. Drop checkpoints mid-task: `node out/cli.js checkpoint "what I'm doing" --project "name"` — if you hit a session cap, the next agent picks up here.

### AFTER LEARNING SOMETHING
10. Call `brain_learn` (MCP) **or** `node out/cli.js learn <type> "title" --project "name"` (CLI) — feed bug fixes, decisions, patterns, gotchas back to the brain.

### LEAVING UNFINISHED WORK
11. Call `brain_handoff` (MCP) **or** `node out/cli.js handoff "Status: X | Next: Y | Files: Z" --to any` (CLI).

### END — DO ALL STEPS, IN ORDER
12. **Commit and push** — see [Commit & Push](#commit--push) below. Non-negotiable.
13. Call `session_end "summary"` (MCP) **or** `node out/cli.js session-end --summary "..."` (CLI) — releases claim.
14. Push brain to GitHub:
    - **Windows:** `pwsh scripts/sync-brain.ps1 -PushOnly`
    - **Linux/Mac:** `bash scripts/sync-brain.sh --push-only`

## Rules

These rules apply to ALL agents without exception.

### Security

1. **No API keys ever** — Never commit `.env` files, tokens, credentials, or secrets. Check `git status` and `git diff` before every commit. If you find exposed keys, remove them immediately and warn via `urgent_set`.

2. **Think OWASP** — XSS, SQL injection, command injection, path traversal. Always use parameterized queries, escape output, sanitize user input. Validate at system boundaries, trust internal code.

3. **Least privilege** — Don't request more permissions, access, or dependencies than the task needs. Close connections, release resources, clean up temp files.

4. **Don't log secrets** — `console.log(config)` can leak API keys into transcripts and logs. Redact sensitive values before output.

### Code Quality

5. **Add insightful comments** — Explain the **WHY**: intent, edge cases, non-obvious constraints, subtle invariants. Don't explain the WHAT — well-named identifiers already do that. One clear line beats a paragraph.

6. **Refactor when it improves clarity** — Simplify, deduplicate, improve structure while keeping behavior identical. Three similar lines is better than a premature abstraction. Don't over-engineer for hypothetical futures.

7. **Prefer guard clauses** — Return early for invalid states, edge cases, and preconditions. Flattens code, reduces nesting, makes the happy path obvious.

8. **Fix root causes, not symptoms** — Don't paper over bugs with workarounds. Trace the issue to its source.

9. **Remove dead code** — Delete it, don't comment it out. Git history preserves it. No half-finished implementations — complete it or handoff.

10. **Prefer editing existing files** over creating new ones. Don't add features, refactors, or abstractions beyond what the task requires.

11. **Before deleting code** — Grep the project and related projects to verify nothing references it. A quick search prevents broken builds.

12. **Don't introduce dependencies** without asking — Every new package is a maintenance burden and widens the security surface. Justify it.

### Error Handling

13. **Fail fast** — Validate inputs at the top of a function. Return or throw immediately with a clear message. Don't let bad data propagate.

14. **Don't swallow errors** — Empty `catch {}` blocks hide bugs. If you must catch, log it or re-throw with context. Every silent catch is a time bomb.

15. **Code the unhappy path** — What happens when the API is down, the file is missing, the response is empty, the user has no permissions? Handle it or explicitly state it's unhandled.

### Naming & Structure

16. **Use descriptive names** — `getUserById` not `get`. If a variable needs a comment to explain what it is, rename it.

17. **One function, one purpose** — If a function "does X and Y" or has "and" in its name, split it.

18. **Don't repeat yourself** — Same logic 3+ times? Extract it. But don't prematurely DRY two things that are coincidentally similar — they may diverge.

19. **Project naming in knowledge/projects/** — Use PascalCase matching the repo/folder name exactly as written on disk (e.g., `TijhaBooks`, `Cognitive1`). Never create a new project file if one already exists with a case-insensitive match — use `project_init` with `action:'update'` instead. Pass `project_name` explicitly; do not rely on `path.basename()` auto-detection when you know the correct casing. If you consolidate duplicate project files, leave a `brain_learn` gotcha recording the merge.

### Type & Data Safety

20. **Avoid `any` in TypeScript** — Use `unknown` if you genuinely don't know the type, then narrow with type guards. Every `any` is a missed bug.

21. **Check for null/undefined** — Use optional chaining (`?.`), nullish coalescing (`??`), and guard clauses before accessing properties.

22. **Be safe with arrays** — Use `.find()` instead of `[0]` when the element might not exist. Check `.length` before indexing.

### Performance

23. **Avoid N+1 queries** — Fetching data in a loop? Batch it. One query for the list is always faster than one query per item.

24. **Don't prematurely optimize** — Make it correct first. Profile before optimizing. Slow correct code beats fast wrong code.

### Simplicity

25. **YAGNI** — You Ain't Gonna Need It. Don't add features, hooks, or interfaces "just in case." Solve the problem in front of you.

26. **Don't solve problems you don't have** — No concurrent writes? Don't add locking. One caller? Don't add an abstraction layer.

27. **Small, incremental changes** — A 5-line change that ships beats a 500-line refactor that might break things. Build, test, commit, repeat.

### Session Discipline

28. **Never self-tag** — No agent names in commits, brain entries, daily logs, or anywhere. Commit messages describe the **change**, not the agent.

29. **Never commit agent folders** — No `.claude/`, `.kilo/`, `.qwen/`, `.continue/`, `.cursor/`, `.kimi/`, `.kimi-code/`. Never commit your own `agents/<name>.md` — user-owned files.

30. **ALWAYS commit and push before session end.** Run `git status`, stage everything relevant, commit with a clear message, then `git push`. Uncommitted work is lost work — this step is non-negotiable.

31. **One logical change per commit** — Focused commits are easier to review, revert, and understand. Don't bundle unrelated changes.

32. **Keep it reversible** — Prefer changes that are easy to undo. If something is risky, checkpoint first.

33. **Leave checkpoints** — `node out/cli.js checkpoint "what I'm doing" --project "name"` mid-task. If you lose connectivity or hit a session cap, the next agent picks up here.

34. **Claim and clear handovers immediately** — When picking up a handoff, delete its entry from `brain/handoffs.md` and commit that deletion before writing a single line of code. An entry still in the file means it is unclaimed. An entry gone means it is yours. Never work on a handoff while its entry still exists — other agents will assume it is available and collide with you.

### Before Touching Code

35. **Read project docs first** — Read `CLAUDE.md`, `README`, and relevant brain entries before working on an unfamiliar project. Don't assume.

36. **Check for active agents** — Call `active_list` before editing a project. If someone else is working there, coordinate — don't collide.

37. **Brain recall before every task — always learn first** — Call `brain_recall "topic"` before every task, no exceptions. The brain is your primary learning tool: every bug, gotcha, and decision recorded there was paid for by a past agent's time. Skipping recall throws that investment away and guarantees you will repeat the same mistakes. Always recall, always learn.

### Testing

38. **Test the feature, not just the types** — `tsc --noEmit` passing doesn't mean the code works. Test the golden path and edge cases manually. If you can't test it, say so explicitly — don't claim success.

39. **Tests document behavior** — Write tests that show what the code should do (behavior), not how it does it. A reader should understand the contract from the test.

40. **Test edge cases** — Empty input, null, maximum values, timeouts, network failures, race conditions. The bugs live in the edges.

### Communication

41. **Respond in English** regardless of input language.

42. **Verify your work** — Run build/lint after changes. Don't leave broken code for the next agent.

43. **Before major refactors** — Explain the plan and get alignment. Don't surprise the user with architectural changes.

44. **If you're uncertain, ask** — Guessing wrong wastes more time than asking. Don't be confidently incorrect.

45. **Handle errors gracefully** — Don't crash with a raw stack trace. Give the user a useful message they can act on.

### Writing Style

46. **No emojis or decorative unicode** — No emojis, decorative unicode characters, or icons in code, code comments, commit messages, documentation, or any written output. Plain text only — unless the user specifically asks for it.

47. **No em-dashes or long dashes** — Do not use em-dashes (—) or en-dashes (–) in any output. Use plain ASCII hyphens (-), commas, semicolons, or sentence breaks instead. Long dashes make text harder to read in monospace terminals and don't exist on standard keyboards.

### Cross-Platform Code

48. **Use `path.join()` for filesystem paths** — Never hardcode `/` or `\`. Let Node handle it per-platform. This repo runs on both Windows and Linux.

49. **Use forward slashes in imports** — `import './utils/foo'` not `'.\utils\foo'`. TypeScript normalizes them but consistency prevents issues.

### Agent Neutrality

50. **Never personalise the product for your own agent** — Do not add features, UI, APIs, defaults, or integrations that favour or require a specific AI agent (Claude, Qwen, Kimi, Copilot, etc.). Every improvement must work identically for any agent. If you catch yourself writing "Claude-only" or "Qwen-preferred" logic, stop and make it agent-agnostic.

51. **Choose agent-independent solutions** — When picking a library, API, pattern, or tool, choose what any agent can use regardless of its provider. Avoid Anthropic SDK, OpenAI SDK, or any vendor-specific client inside the cognitive1 core unless the feature is explicitly a per-vendor adapter behind a neutral interface. The brain, session system, and all shared infrastructure are vendor-neutral by design — keep them that way.

### Cross-OS Development

52. **Check `updates.md` on session start** — This repo is worked on from both Windows and Linux. The `out/` directory (compiled JS) is not committed. When an agent on one OS adds or changes source files, it documents the change in `updates.md`. Agents on the other OS must check this file on session start and run the listed action before touching anything.

53. **Document new features in `updates.md`** — After completing a feature that changes source files, configuration, or the dashboard, add an entry to `updates.md` with: date, OS, what changed, key files, and the action the other OS needs to take. Mark your OS as done. Delete entries once both OSes have applied them.

54. **Build actions by change type:**
    - New or modified `.ts` files: `npm run build` (always enough unless deps changed)
    - Modified `package.json` or new imports of uninstalled packages: `npm install && npm run build`
    - Dashboard changes only: no build needed (the daemon serves `dashboard/index.html` directly)
    - Config changes (`config.ts`): `npm run build`

### Brain Hygiene

55. **Keep the brain updated** — Stale knowledge is worse than none. If a bug is fixed, mark it resolved. If a pattern changes, update it. Run `brain_prune` periodically.

56. **Feed the brain after every session** — At minimum, leave a handoff with status and next steps. Learning compounds over time.

57. **Keep the brain clean** — Record only reusable knowledge. Git-commit mirroring is disabled; git log already records that. Don't bloat the brain with entries that duplicate what version control already tracks.

## MCP Tools Reference

For agents with native MCP support (Claude Code, Cursor via MCP, Copilot with MCP plugin, etc.).

| Tool | When to call |
|------|--------------|
| `session_start` | Session start — auto-claims project, delivers briefing with this file |
| `session_end` | Session end — releases claim, logs summary |
| `brain_recall` | Before every task — search bugs, gotchas, decisions |
| `brain_learn` | After fixing a bug, making a decision, discovering a pattern |
| `brain_handoff` | Leaving unfinished work for the next agent |
| `brain_prune` | Periodic cleanup of stale brain entries |
| `brain_stats` | See what agents have been contributing |
| `brain_status` | Brain health overview |
| `active_list` | Before editing — see who's working on what |
| `active_claim` | Claim focused work on a specific project |
| `active_release` | Release a claim when done without calling session_end |
| `urgent_set` | Block other agents from a dangerous or in-progress area |
| `urgent_list` | Check for active blocks before starting |
| `urgent_clear` | Clear an urgent block once the risk is resolved |
| `wiki_status` | Full system dashboard |
| `task_create` | Create a tracked task |
| `task_list` | List open tasks |
| `task_claim` | Claim a task to work on |
| `task_complete` | Mark a task done |
| `recall` | Fast search alias — equivalent to brain_recall |
| `project_init` | Bootstrap a new project with Cognitive1 integration |
| `compliance_audit` | Audit projects for integration compliance |
| `decision_log` | Record a structured architectural decision with alternatives |
| `regression_log` | Log test results after changes; detects regressions |
| `cost_log` / `cost_report` | Track token spend across agents |

## CLI Quick Reference

For agents without native MCP support. Run from the cognitive1 project root.

```bash
# Session lifecycle
node out/cli.js session-start
node out/cli.js session-end --summary "what was done"

# Brain access
node out/cli.js recall "query"
node out/cli.js learn bugs "title" --project "name" --tags "tag1,tag2"
node out/cli.js learn gotchas "title" --project "name"
node out/cli.js learn decisions "title" --project "name"
node out/cli.js learn patterns "title" --project "name"

# Handoffs and checkpoints
node out/cli.js handoff "Status: X | Next: Y | Files: Z" --to any
node out/cli.js checkpoint "what I'm doing" --project "name"
node out/cli.js recover

# Status
node out/cli.js status
node out/cli.js active-list
```

## Commit & Push

**Required before every session end.** No exceptions.

```bash
git status                              # Always check first — catch unstaged files and secrets
git add <specific files>               # Stage specifically — never blindly add -A without checking
git commit -m "describe the change"    # What changed and why, not which agent did it
git push
```

Rules:
- One logical change per commit. Don't bundle unrelated edits.
- Commit messages describe the **change**, never the agent.
- Never commit `.env`, credentials, or agent config folders.
- If in doubt whether to commit a file, check `git diff <file>` first.

All rules above apply to every agent. The following additional rules apply per agent type:

## Cognitive1 Connection

Daemon runs at `http://localhost:9876`. MCP-capable agents connect automatically via the project `.mcp.json`.

**Windows:**
```powershell
pwsh scripts/sync-brain.ps1 -PullOnly    # Pull brain at session start
node out/cli.js session-start             # Or use MCP session_start tool
pwsh scripts/sync-brain.ps1 -PushOnly    # Push brain at session end
```

**Linux/Mac:**
```bash
bash scripts/sync-brain.sh --pull-only
node out/cli.js session-start
bash scripts/sync-brain.sh --push-only
```
